title: Annotatio III §.II: Zurich reply (German) — joy at Luther’s answer; Capito and Bucer’s report; Basel Confession accepted; unity on Word, Baptism, and Supper without empty signs — Hucusque Tigurini
pass_a_gloss: Honorable, highly learned in Christ, especially beloved Lord and Friend: we have received your friendly and kind-hearted Answer — which you sent us in recent days to the Writing we made to you toward Schmalkalden — with highest joy and rejoicing to God our heavenly Father ... And since we can understand not otherwise, not only from your Writing but also from the faithful opening and report of our especially beloved Lords, Friends and Brothers, Dr. Capito and Bucer, who were with us that day, than that you mean well and good the business of this holy Unity ... and likewise that you take in good pleasure our Confession drawn up at Basel together with the Declaration that followed on it ... Since also concerning the Articles of the outward Word and Baptism we see that Your Honor finds no misunderstanding ... and beside that, on the Article of the holy Sacrament of the Body and Blood of Christ, we understand that you have never taught, and still do not teach, that Christ comes down and goes up from heaven, from the right hand of God his Father ... and so you set no Presence or eating of Christ’s Body and Blood in the holy Supper from which something would follow contrary to the true Incarnation and Ascension of Christ ... we also on the other side do not want that in the Supper only bare or empty signs, but also the Body and Blood of the Lord, be received and enjoyed — so that this in itself is truly grasped and received only through the believing mind ... therefore we can now see and find nothing else than that we (God have praise) are one with each other in understanding and right substance, and unto good peace, and that there is no more dispute between us ... Full page Hh / Thus far the words of the Zurichers,
pass_b_english: The Zurich letter opens: Honorable, highly learned friend in Christ — we received with highest joy your kind answer to the writing we sent you toward Schmalkalden, thanking our heavenly Father.

From your letter and from Capito and Bucer’s faithful report while they were with us, we can only take it that you mean this holy unity well, and that you gladly accept our Basel Confession with the Declaration that followed.

On the outward Word and Baptism you find no misunderstanding; on the holy Sacrament of Christ’s body and blood we gather you have never taught — and do not teach — a descent or ascent from the Father’s right hand that would set a presence or eating in the Supper contrary to the true incarnation and ascension.

We for our part refuse bare empty signs in the Supper: the Lord’s body and blood are received, yet truly grasped only by the believing mind, as our Confession and Declaration sent to Schmalkalden still hold.
So we now see nothing else than that — God be praised — we are one in understanding and right substance, at peace, with no dispute left between us. (Full page Hh.) Thus far the Zurichers’ words.
source_text: Ehrwürdiger Hochgelahrter in Christo / w. sonders geliebter Herr und Freund / wir haben euere freundliche und gutherzige Antwort / die ihr uns auf das Schreiben / welches wir euch gen Schmalkalden gethan / verschienen Tagen zugesandt / mit höchster Freud und Frolocken zu GOtt unserm himlischen Vater / empfangen / ... Und dieweil wir den nicht allein aus eurem Schreiben / sondern auch der hochgelehrten unserer insonders geliebten Herrn / Freunde und Brüdern / D. Capitonis und Buceri ... nicht anders verstehen können / denn das ihr den Handel dieser heiligen Einigkeit wol und gut meinet / ... desgleichen auch unser zu Basel gestellete Confeßion / zu sampt der darauff gefolgten Declaration ... zu gutem gefallen annemet / ... Dieweil wir auch der Artickel halben vom eufferlichen Wort und Tauffe / sehen / das E.E. keinen Misverstand findet / ... und daneben bey dem Artickel des heiligen Sacraments des Leibs und Bluts Christi verstanden / das ihr noch nie gelehret habt / auch noch nicht lehret / daß Christus vom Himmel / von der rechten Hand Gottes seines Vaters hernieder und auffahre ... und also keine Gegenwärtigkeit / oder Niessung des Leibes und Bluts Christi im heiligen Abendmahl setzet / aus der etwas folgete / das der wahren Menschwerdung und Himmelfahrt Christi ... wiedrig ... wir auch dagegen nicht wollen / das im Abendmahl allein blosse oder leere zeichen / sondern auch der Leib und das Blut des HErrn empfangen und genossen werde / also / das dis an ihm selbst allein durch das gläubige Gemuth warlich begriffen und empfangen werde / ... so können wir numehr nicht anders sehen noch befinden / denn das wir / (Gott hab Lob) im Verstande und rechter substanz mit einander einig / und zu gutem Frieden / auch kein Streit mehr zwischen uns sey ... Pag. integra Hh / Hucusque verba Tigurinorum,
notes: Hexades Annotatio III §.II densify §207; German Zurich reply condensed through Hucusque Tigurinorum.
